recent.question: Will Bitcoin dip to $84,000 on October 6?
recent.what_happened: Late on Oct 6 ET (early Oct 7 UTC), BTC fell below $84,000 on Binance to about $83,966 in a fast liquidation cascade that wiped out roughly $360M of longs in about 10 minutes, so the market resolved YES.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecaster's own base rate showed sub-$84k Binance prints on at least 4–5 of the previous ~14 days, with Oct 1 and Oct 3 both included. It also showed repeated rejections near $87k, record-high yields, ETF outflows, and documented 2% drops inside 30 minutes, yet it went down to 10%, close to the 9% market price. The jev_alone (0.30) and claude_direct (0.27) forecasts were better calibrated.
recent.lesson: If the strike is under 2% away with most of a 24h window left, and recent days crossed the same level about 30% of the time, don't drop below roughly 20–25% just because the price is currently quiet or the market is cheap.

suggested_change.change: For intraday crypto touch markets, flag any forecast that falls more than 15 points below the empirical touch frequency over the last 14 days, and require a stated reason before accepting it.

recent.question: Will Ciara Miller and their partner be eliminated from Dancing with the Stars Season 35 before Oct 7, 2026?
recent.what_happened: On the Oct 6 Mariah Carey Night show (Week 4), Ciara Miller and Brandon Armstrong danced a jazz to "Emotions" and scored 21/30. They were the one couple sent home after combined judges' scores and viewer votes, so the market resolved YES.
recent.what_we_missed: Almost every fact in the research was about Jackson Olson and Emma Slater, not Ciara Miller. That includes his scores, his bottom-three finish in Week 3, his Waltz assignment and his partner's injury. The only fact about Miller was a Week 3 score of 18, in the bottom half of the group. We never checked whether she had been in jeopardy before or how strong her fan vote was, so the 21% was built on another contestant's profile. With one of 12 couples going home, 21% was still a fair price, and correct research might not have pushed it much past the market.
recent.lesson: Before forecasting, check that every status and event fact names the contestant in the question and their own pro partner (here Brandon Armstrong). Treat a mismatch as a reason to redo the research, not to forecast anyway.

suggested_change.change: Add a check that rejects the fact set when most facts name a different contestant or partner than the question, and send it back for new research.

recent.question: Los Angeles D wins
recent.what_happened: The Dodgers won Game 3 in Atlanta. It was a near coin-flip matchup between Yamamoto and Sale, and the market had it at 50.5%. All our forecasts fell between 0.47 and 0.53, so the outcome was within normal variance. I couldn't find any game details that would have shifted the odds before first pitch.
recent.what_we_missed: Nothing important. The evidence was mixed: the Braves won the regular-season series and Sale was rested and pitching at home, but Sale's career postseason ERA is 5.83 and the Dodgers had better recent form. Only jev_with_research (0.53) leaned the right way. Even so, the bold strategy lost about $1,497, which suggests it took a large position against the Dodgers on a near-50/50 game.
recent.lesson: When our estimate is within about 3 points of a roughly 50% market price, we have no real edge, so we should skip the bet or keep it small.

suggested_change.change: Cap bet size for the bold strategy, or block the bet entirely, when the model's probability differs from the market price by less than about 5 points and the different forecasts don't agree on a direction.

recent.question: Antigua and Barbuda wins
recent.what_happened: Antigua and Barbuda beat Aruba at home at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in the last group game, so the market resolved Yes. I couldn't find the final score or match details in my search.
recent.what_we_missed: Antigua were at home in a must-win game, coming off 5-0 and 3-0 wins and with only one goal conceded all campaign. The 1-0 loss to Aruba on Sep 23 came from a stoppage-time header, so it was close. The forecast leaned too hard on that result and on Aruba's 9 points, and came in below the market's 0.415.
recent.lesson: In evenly matched minnow fixtures, don't let a narrow, late-goal head-to-head loss push the home team below the market price, especially when the home team needs the win and is in better recent form.

suggested_change.change: No process change needed. The 0.36 forecast was a reasonable call on a near coin-flip match, though it could have stayed closer to the market price.

recent.question: Will MrBeast's next video get at least 45 million views on day 1?
recent.what_happened: The question resolved YES: 'Eat Everything In A Grocery Store Win $1,000,000' premiered on Saturday, Oct 3, 2026, and passed 45M views within its first 24 hours. My one search did not find a published day-1 total, but the YES outcome confirms it got there. It was the sequel to the April 'Last To Leave Grocery Store' video, which went viral, and MrBeast had promoted it all week as a 'mini movie.'
recent.what_we_missed: The forecast was made about 5 hours after the video went up, at roughly 21:00 UTC, when its live view count could already be checked. The market's 0.87 almost certainly reflected that early pace. Our team instead relied on unverified base rates from philanthropy and other videos, which put day 1 in the mid-20s to low 30s of millions. We gave too little weight to the sequel effect, the week of hype, and a 518M-subscriber channel.
recent.lesson: If the video is already live when you judge a view-count market, check its current view count and how fast it is climbing before using historical base rates. A market price far from yours (0.87 against 0.42) usually means it has live data you don't.

suggested_change.change: For time-window view-count markets, require research to fetch the target video's current views and hours since posting, and extrapolate from that pace, whenever the video is already live.

recent.question: Chicago WS wins
recent.what_happened: The White Sox came back from 0-2 down to beat Cleveland 4-3 at Progressive Field in ALDS Game 2 and lead the series 2-0. Opener Anthony Kay was followed by Sean Burke, who allowed one hit in 4⅔ innings of bulk relief. Braden Montgomery's two-run double in the 6th gave Chicago the lead, and Grant Taylor closed out the 9th.
recent.what_we_missed: We didn't miss much. Our 0.50 was above the market's 0.405 and leaned the right way. The research did flag Venable's opener/bulk plan for Burke. What it didn't anticipate was that Grant Taylor would be available to close despite throwing 4 innings in Game 1.
recent.lesson: When a road team is close to evenly matched, has momentum, and has a believable plan for its pitching staff, a near-50% forecast above a market around 40% is reasonable. Don't push toward the home-favorite price just because of seeding.

suggested_change.change: No process change is needed. This is a well-calibrated forecast that came out on the side we leaned toward. Sources: https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/white-sox-vs-guardians-updates-170048164.html, https://www.foxsports.com/mlb/alds-game-2-chicago-white-sox-vs-cleveland-guardians-oct-05-2026-game-boxscore-97203

recent_wins.question: Will Mexico win on 2026-10-05?
recent_wins.what_happened: The friendly was played on October 6, 2026 at the LA Memorial Coliseum, one day after the date in the question. Chile beat Mexico 2-0 with goals from Maximiliano Gutiérrez (56') and Vicente Pizarro (66'). That left Mexico without a win in four games under Rafa Márquez, and the market resolved No.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research forecast moved from 0.40 to 0.16 on real warning signs: Mexico had won none of three games under Márquez, had leaked goals against the US, was missing four players (Mora, Chávez, Lozano, Romo), and might change goalkeepers. It also correctly noted that a draw counts as No. Still, nothing found before kickoff decided the game. A pro-Mexico crowd in LA against a Chile team that had lost both of its window games made Mexico's win chance roughly 45-60%, so 0.16 was far too confident and mostly got lucky against the market's 0.625.
recent_wins.lesson: If the forecast differs from the market by more than 30 points and no decisive fact (lineup collapse, rule quirk, known result) is behind it, pull it back toward the market. Poor form and injuries in a friendly don't justify a 4-to-1 call against the favourite.

suggested_change.change: Add a check that flags any forecast more than 30 points from the market unless the research cites a specific fact that decides the outcome, and caps how big a bet it can drive.

recent_wins.question: Will Jackson Olson and their partner be eliminated from Dancing with the Stars Season 35 before Oct 7, 2026?
recent_wins.what_happened: On Mariah Carey Night (Oct 6), Jackson Olson and Emma Slater danced a Waltz to 'Without You' and scored 21/30, their best score so far. Only Ciara Miller and Brandon Armstrong were eliminated, so Olson stayed in and the question resolved No.
recent_wins.what_worked: The forecast saw that only one live show fell inside the window and that every episode so far had sent home just one couple. That left one elimination among 12 couples. Olson was weak but not clearly the weakest: Guillermo Rodriguez kept scoring lower, and Ciara Miller had tied Olson at 18. So a probability around 22% made sense. The market's 61.5% was an overreaction to Olson being in the bottom three in Week 3.
recent_wins.lesson: For single-episode elimination markets, start from 1 divided by the number of couples left (times the eliminations expected that night), then adjust for judges' scores and bottom-three history. Being in the bottom three once rarely justifies a price above 50% when several other couples score as low or lower.

suggested_change.change: Always pull a full scoreboard of who has been in the bottom two or three and who has the lowest scores, plus how many eliminations are expected per episode, so the forecast can measure how weak the contestant really is against the rest of the field.

recent_wins.question: Will over 5.5 goals be scored? (Over 5.5 goals scored)
recent_wins.what_happened: Argentina beat Benin 3-0 at the Más Monumental in Messi's farewell game. Otamendi and Nico Paz scored, and Messi added a penalty. With 3 goals, Over 5.5 lost and the market resolved NO.
recent_wins.what_worked: The forecaster went with the base rate: 2 of Argentina's last 6 home friendlies had 6 or more goals, and Benin is a competent AFCON side under Rohr that rarely concedes heavily. It did not chase the 7-0 against a weakened Burkina Faso side, so it priced YES at 0.39, below the market's 0.455. Still, 0.39 means it gave YES almost a 40% chance, and the actual margin (3 goals) says little about whether 0.39 was better calibrated than the market. Much of the credit goes to taking the cheaper side of a call that was always uncertain.
recent_wins.lesson: For high goal lines in friendlies, start from the team's base rate and check whether the opponent is at full strength (Benin was, Burkina Faso had sent a weakened side). Don't extrapolate from a blowout that a depleted opponent explains.

suggested_change.change: Have the research step flag whether a team's most recent blowout came against a depleted or weakened opponent, and compare that opponent's strength with the upcoming one, so recency doesn't inflate over-goal estimates.

recent_wins.question: Tyler Shough: 250+ passing yards
recent_wins.what_happened: On Monday Night Football the Falcons beat the Saints 45-24. Shough threw for 286 yards, including a late touchdown to Devaughn Vele, which cleared the 250 line by 36 yards.
recent_wins.what_worked: Research raised the forecast from 0.32 to 0.75 using current-season facts: about 44 attempts and 305 yards per game, 250+ in all three 2026 starts, Atlanta ranked 29th in passing yards allowed, and Etienne on IR, which made a pass-heavy plan more likely. The lopsided loss also helped, since trailing teams pass more and much of Shough's yardage likely came late, so part of the margin came from how the game went.
recent_wins.lesson: For QB yardage props, look at current-season attempt volume, the opponent's pass-defense rank and injuries in the QB's own backfield rather than older career game logs. A team that is likely to trail, or has lost its running backs, will tend to throw more, which supports the over.

suggested_change.change: Always pull the QB's current-season attempts per game, the opponent's pass-defense rank and the game spread, and give these more weight than last season's splits, because the no-research forecast (0.32) leaned on the 2025 log and missed.

recent_wins.question: Brian Robinson: 50+ rushing yards
recent_wins.what_happened: Atlanta beat New Orleans 45-24. Brian Robinson Jr., Bijan Robinson's backup, ran for 62 yards and 3 touchdowns, so the market resolved YES. Bijan ran for 145 yards on 19 carries.
recent_wins.what_worked: Very little of the research applied. Every player fact was about Bijan Robinson, a different player from the Brian Robinson named in the market. That error pushed the forecast up to 0.64. Only two facts were relevant to Brian: the Saints' run defense ranked 27th and Atlanta's run game ranked 2nd. That matchup left room for a backup to get carries, and a 45-24 blowout delivered them.
recent_wins.lesson: Before using any stats, check that the player in the research matches the player in the market's name exactly. Brian Robinson Jr. is not Bijan Robinson. Also treat a market price near 0.20 for a star's 50-yard line as a sign you may have the wrong player.

suggested_change.change: Add a gate that blocks a bet when the full name in the researched facts doesn't match the market's player name, or when the forecast differs from a liquid player-prop price by more than about 3x without a stated reason.

recent_wins.question: New York Y wins
recent_wins.what_happened: The Rays beat the Yankees 5-2 in ALDS Game 2 at Tropicana Field and took a 2-0 series lead. The Yankees made four errors, three of them on the first four batters Cam Schlittler faced, and three of Tampa Bay's five runs were unearned. Freddy Peralta allowed one run in 4 2/3 innings.
recent_wins.what_worked: The researched forecast leaned against the Yankees at 0.38 while the market had them at 0.535. Its reasons were real: the Rays had home field, Aaron Judge was off the roster, Peralta was in top form, and Tampa Bay's pitching had just held New York scoreless. But the Yankees didn't lose on any of those. They lost on fielding mistakes nobody could forecast, against the best road starter in MLB, so the result mostly reflects how random a single baseball game is.
recent_wins.lesson: For a single MLB game, treat a 15-point gap from the market as low-confidence unless the research turns up a concrete edge, such as a lineup or injury change the market hasn't priced. Don't count a win like this one as proof the method works.

suggested_change.change: Shrink single-game MLB forecasts toward the market price, which was close to 50/50 here, unless the research cites a specific fact the market hasn't absorbed, and cap bet size in those cases.

rules.rule: Read crypto rules for the exact strike, venue/pair (e.g. Binance BTC/USDT) and test (any touch or a close at a set candle), restate the strike up top, measure each price fact against it, and record a timestamped spot from that venue under an hour old for same-day windows.

For crypto threshold questions, report percent distance to strike, hours left, how many of the last 14 days the venue traded through that level, realized volatility, any weekend, and timestamped same-day catalysts (yields, dollar, ETF flows, jobs data) or state none found.

When judged mid-window, first check whether the strike was already reached inside the window: cite dated reports of the high and its margin past the strike, confirm on the resolution venue's candles where possible, and treat earlier-week moves as background.

For single-match win questions, confirm in the rules whether only a regulation-time win counts and state that a draw resolves No; check the actual venue, since a listed home side may play at a neutral ground, and report each side's results in this competition.

For match questions, report the current-season head-to-head with its game count (under about 10 games is small; note source disagreements) and each side's dated, sourced absences and returns; when injury sources disagree, check the confirmed matchday squad or lineup.
Discard any search snippet claiming a match result that is undated or dated before kickoff; report a result only from sources published after the match was played.

For match goal-total questions, report each team's recent comparable match totals with dates, note whether opponents in any blowout were weakened or missing starters, and compare that with the upcoming opponent's squad strength.

For tennis completion questions, read which endings count, report the tour level's normal-finish share and each player's recent full matches, weigh only past-week injury or withdrawal news, and after start time check Tennis Explorer or ITF for w/o or ret. first.

For NFL player props, use only the named player's facts: for TDs, rushing vs receiving, share of carries or targets inside the 5, multi-season TD-game rate; for yardage, current-season attempts per game, games past the line, opponent's rank against it, backfield injuries.

For single MMA fights, report each fighter's age, recent opponents and how those fights ended, and dated weigh-in or weight-cut news; label win streaks and common-opponent comparisons as weak evidence.

For single MLB games, report both confirmed starters' season ERA and ERA+ and recent starts, each team's season record, late-season form (record and offense since Sept 1) and home field; if it is a bullpen game, note that an opener's few innings carry little weight.

For playoff series and games, give the series score, what the trailing team still needs and where, earlier games' margins, current-season records and head-to-head, and whether standing rests on seeding; label past seasons' playoff records as small-sample background.

For in-round golf leader questions, pull the live hole-by-hole leaderboard and, for the named player and everyone within about 3 shots, report score, holes left and tee wave, plus the field's scoring average and how the rules settle a tie for the lead.

For golf tournament winner questions, report the player's world ranking, pro starts and wins, the field's strength and size, and his prior-week schedule (e.g. a team event); label team-event results and a single pro win as weak evidence of dominance.

For video view questions, record when the question opened and check the channel's upload list for any video posted since; if one is live, report its upload time, hours elapsed, current views and climb rate before any historical base rates, plus sequel or promotion context.

For view-count bracket questions, build reference figures only from first-168-hour counts of the channel's recent comparable uploads; label cumulative or lifetime totals, figures with unclear snapshot dates, and months-old uploads as not the resolution metric.

For Rotten Tomatoes score questions, read the year-specific film page named in the rules, record the score, review count and dated earlier readings showing drift, and count how many negative reviews would move it past the strike before the check time.

For reality-show elimination questions, confirm every fact names the asked contestant and their own pro partner, and report couples left, eliminations per episode, live shows in the window, and every couple's judges' scores and bottom-three history.

For multi-seat or multi-candidate elections, report alongside polls the undecided share, joint tickets and endorsements, late dropouts and whom they backed, whether one side's vote splits across candidates, and dated past gaps between final polls and results there.

Take counts and base rates from a cited source covering the current format to the latest event, using the resolution's named provider and its counting method first (e.g. its trailing 2–4 weeks); label recalled, disputed or roughly dozen-case counts as unverified.

proposals.title: Main demands a bigger edge
proposals.why: Jev + research trails the market by about 0.06 Brier on 559 paired markets, so many of its 8c 'edges' are probably forecast error. Main loses about $26 per $100 since the floor (11 settled) and trails original per dollar on the yardstick (-$32 vs -$22 per $100). Requiring 12c, as claude_direct now does, tests whether fewer, stronger-conviction bets lose less. This is an experiment on small numbers.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, main's P&L per $100 staked on the yardstick (shared markets) is better than original's over the same period, and better than main's since-floor -$26 per $100. If main places fewer than 10 bets in a week, revert to 0.08.

proposals.title: Price breakdown since each strategy's last rule change
proposals.why: by_price_paid is all-time, so pre-floor long shots dominate it: about $100k of losses on 73 bets. That hides whether 30-60c and 60c+ bets pay under the current rules. Bold's -$5.5k and calibrated's +$5.0k in favourites can't be dated to a rule version.
proposals.judge_by: The review shows since-change wins and P&L per price bucket for every strategy, and the next favourites or max_ask decision cites it.

proposals.title: Sports-only Claude gets more bets
proposals.why: Sports is the only category where any forecaster beats the market (Claude 0.158 vs market 0.176, on 131 markets), yet ch16 has placed 1 bet in about 2.5 days. The 4 markets stopped only by Jev's info gate would have paid +$77 per $100. Jev's own information rating may say little about Claude's forecast. This is an experiment on tiny numbers.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, ch16's P&L per $100 staked is positive and ahead of claude_direct's over the same period.

proposals.title: Calibrated vs main on the same markets
proposals.why: Calibrated's profit (+$3.4k on 9 settled since the floor) contrasts with its Brier of 0.210, slightly worse than raw Jev + research at 0.2065. So its edge may come from which bets it picks and how it sizes them, or it may be luck. A paired comparison would show whether the calibration itself earns money before anyone considers moving main onto it.
proposals.judge_by: Report calibrated's and main's P&L per $100 on markets both bet, and on markets only one bet, since 2026-10-01. If calibrated is ahead by more than $10 per $100 on the shared markets after 30 resolved, consider giving main the calibrated forecasts.

proposals.title: Jev alone, bold stops buying favourites

retro.headline: A quiet half-day: 12 new bets, nothing decisive, and the market price still forecasts better than all of our sources (Brier 0.152 vs Claude 0.185 and Jev + research 0.212 on the same 559 markets).
went_well: Favourites priced 60c and up keep paying for the calibrated Jev forecasts. Calibrated is 8 for 8 there (+$5.9k), and the favourites-only challenger ch13 is 2 for 2 (+$2.2k). That is 10 bets in total, so it is still an experiment, not a finding.

Jev alone, bold is +$2.3k on 9 settled bets since it stopped buying above 60c. Bold is +$0.6k on 20 settled since it started skipping crypto. Both are roughly break-even or better, but both rest on fewer than 30 results.
Coin-flip bets (30-60c) are slightly positive for three strategies: main +$0.9k on 16, bold +$1.8k on 41, Jev alone bold +$1.1k on 20. The 30c floor is removing the worst of the losses.
went_badly: Main is behind the yardstick per dollar. On shared markets since original started, main loses $32 per $100 staked (-$14.2k on 22 settled) and original loses $22 per $100 (-$14.6k on 31 settled). Main's tuning has not paid so far.
Main is -$5.6k on 11 settled since the floor went in (5 wins), about -$26 per $100. The floor removed long shots but did not make main's 30c+ bets profitable.

Calibrated's coin flips lose: -$4.5k on 12 (5 wins). Claude direct is -$14.9k all time and has settled only 2 bets under its stricter 12c edge rule. Jev alone has placed 1 bet ever, so it teaches us nothing.

ideas_for_joey.title: Break results down by price paid
ideas_for_joey.why: Many losses, including all 3 of claude_direct's and every info-gate-stopped group, show -$100 per $100, meaning the whole stake was lost. That pattern suggests we may be buying cheap longshots. A breakdown of wins and P&L by ask price (for example <0.2, 0.2–0.5, 0.5–0.8, >0.8), for placed and stopped bets, would let us set min_ask and max_ask from evidence instead of guessing.

ideas_for_joey.title: Score forecasters on 30c+ markets only
ideas_for_joey.why: Since 2026-10-01 every strategy bets only at 30c or more, but the Brier table (market 0.114 vs our best 0.121) mixes in the long shots we no longer touch. We need to know whether any forecaster beats the price where we actually bet, matched market by market.

ideas_for_joey.title: Shrink forecasts toward the market before computing edge
ideas_for_joey.why: The market's Brier (0.123, 201 markets) beats every forecaster, and most of our losses came from bets where we disagreed with it most, such as long shots that went 1 for 21. A strategy option that blends the forecast with the market price (for example 50/50) before the edge check would bet only where a disagreement survives that discount. The forecasters themselves would still never see the price.

ideas_for_joey.title: Gate ledger and price breakdown for 30c+ markets only
ideas_for_joey.why: The gate ledger mixes in long shots, which lost 1 in 42 before the floor. That makes every 'stopped by the info gate' number look worse than it would under today's rules: calibrated's info-stopped markets show −$7.1 per $100 (66) and main's −$24.6 (78). We can't sensibly tune the info gates until the ledger shows only markets the 30c floor would let through.

ideas_for_joey.title: Pooled tally of bets placed under the floor
ideas_for_joey.why: Each strategy has 0–1 settled bets since 2026-10-01, so the floor's '30 settled bets' test will take weeks per strategy. Pooling every strategy's 30c+ bets placed since the floor, measured against original's long shots over the same period, would answer whether the floor pays much sooner.

ideas_for_joey.title: Claimed edge vs realised return
ideas_for_joey.why: Every source is worse than the market, yet each bet claims at least 8c of edge. Bucketing settled 30c+ bets by claimed edge (8-12c, 12-20c, 20c+) and showing win rate and P&L per $100 would show whether big claimed edges are real edges or big errors. That would tell us whether to raise or lower min_edge.

ideas_for_joey.title: Calibrated vs main on the same markets
ideas_for_joey.why: Calibrated's profit (+$3.4k on 9 settled since the floor) contrasts with its Brier of 0.210, slightly worse than raw Jev + research at 0.2065. So its edge may come from which bets it picks and how it sizes them, or it may be luck. A paired comparison would show whether the calibration itself earns money before anyone considers moving main onto it.

ideas_for_joey.title: Price breakdown since each strategy's last rule change
ideas_for_joey.why: by_price_paid is all-time, so pre-floor long shots dominate it: about $100k of losses on 73 bets. That hides whether 30-60c and 60c+ bets pay under the current rules. Bold's -$5.5k and calibrated's +$5.0k in favourites can't be dated to a rule version.
